subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots continue inheriting all OpenClaw host overrides, or should OpenClaw scope/exclude overrides like `path-to-regexp` when they conflict with plugin-owned dependency graphs?
rationale: The current behavior is a real plugin crash path, but changing override propagation affects OpenClaw's dependency-security policy and existing managed install behavior; a blanket downgrade conflicts with the current Express 5/router dependency contract.

options.title: Scope Managed Overrides
options.body: Keep host security pins where they are safe, but exclude or qualify override propagation when it breaks plugin-owned dependency ranges such as Express 4.x `path-to-regexp` 0.1.x.

options.title: Validator And Docs Only
options.body: Add Express 4.x conflict detection with an actionable error while leaving all host override propagation unchanged, accepting that plugin authors still own the override or Express 5 migration.

options.title: Blanket Downgrade
options.body: Force `path-to-regexp` 0.1.x centrally for plugin roots, which risks conflicting with OpenClaw's Express 5/router stack unless the scoping boundary is proven first.

recommendation.title: Scope Managed Overrides
recommendation.body: Keep host security pins where they are safe, but exclude or qualify override propagation when it breaks plugin-owned dependency ranges such as Express 4.x `path-to-regexp` 0.1.x.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history ties this login to the managed-root override propagation and dependency pin policy most directly involved in the decision.
